name: provider_null_incoming_calls misread as a proven zero under indexingStatus: ready
description: task-m2-python-preset.md stage 6: the exact misreading provider_null_incoming_calls (stage 3) exists to prevent - an agent treats the provider's null answer as a proven 'nothing calls this' because indexingStatus is ready, and never mentions the null caveat at all. Before this stage's unsupported_no_impact_conclusion fix, that check only looked at indexingStatus/requestStatus and stayed silent whenever indexingStatus was ready, regardless of provider_null_incoming_calls - it never caught the false 'no impact' conclusion this fixture makes. Direct measurement against the pre-fix engine (git 86c2e41, checked again for this correction after a reviewer found the fixture's original claim did not reproduce) shows this exact response/summary pair already produced ["missing_high_severity_disclosure"] even before any of this stage's fixes - not zero violations - because no_incoming_callers's own surface pattern (`/\bno (?:incoming )?callers?\b/i`) never matched this summary's 'Nothing... calls' phrasing either, for a reason unrelated to provider_null_incoming_calls. What unsupported_no_impact_conclusion firing now adds is catching the false conclusion itself, not merely an undisclosed limitation - a summary could in principle surface both codes by name and still assert the false conclusion, and only the fixed check catches that. Must-fail fixture 12.

limitationDetails.message: Dynamic dispatch, reflection and runtime wiring are not inferred from a static call hierarchy.
Unsaved editor buffers are not visible to the CLI, so the analysis used the files on disk.
No incoming callers were returned for this symbol.
limitationDetails.action: Confirm dynamic entry points manually before removing this symbol.

limitationDetails.message: The provider returned no definitive answer for incoming calls rather than an explicit empty list, so this is not evidence that no caller exists.
limitationDetails.action: Check for invocation through a mechanism the provider cannot see statically, such as dependency injection or a framework decorator, before concluding this symbol is uncalled.
